emails.subject: RE: [ Ticket: 1298587 ] US00099 I need  to see the windows for the PPI on the X product.
emails.body:
The XP-Detection is being triggered, when either the upper light gate is interrupted, or if the lower light gate is interrupted for a longer distance than the configured parameter for "cleat_width" in the ACS config.  Can we set the condition to “IF BOTH LIGHT GATE TRIGGER” for the X-Products Alarm to be active?

As the central belt cleats trigger the lower light gate when they pass, the software ignores any interruptions of the lower light gate, which are shorter than the configured threshold, usually the actual cleat width + 15mm.
In your case, the cleat width is currently configured at 30mm.

> KSCPConfigurator3 printAll acs_config.kscp | grep -i cleat_width
/CONTROL/Single_Multiline/HAS_XPRODUCT_DETECT/XPRODUCT_CLEAT_WIDTH/ = '30'
<09:39-Thu Mar 09>-<-bash-0>-<knapp @ AUT1 @ ABDC Phoenix>-</etc/knapp/acs>

The length of a detected XProduct is being determined by the amount of pulses of the central belt it is being detected for. The pulse length for your central belt has been measured to be 2.002489mm, which means the XProduct detection is triggered,
whenever the lower light gate is interrupted for more than 15 pulses of the central belt.

> KSCPConfigurator3 printAll acs_config.kscp | grep -i pulse_length
/CORE/ORDERWINDOWCALCULATOR/SYSTEM/PULSE_LENGTH/ = '2.002489'
<09:46-Thu Mar 09>-<-bash-0>-<knapp @ AUT1 @ ABDC Phoenix>-</etc/knapp/acs>

We could in theory increase the configured cleat width and therefore make the XProduct detection less precise, but the downside are possible false negatives, which would lead to customers potentially receiving extra or too few products with their order.
You mentioned earlier that the medication leaflets, which get stuck on the belt, are much smaller than the dimensions of your actual products, but this is only the case if you expect the product to always lay flat on the belt.
If, for example, a rater flat cubic product lies half on a cleat, and therefore on one corner on the bottom of the belt, it makes sense that the XP detection is very precise,
because in such an instance the product might not be detected if we increase the configured cleat width.

As we have discussed earlier, it makes sense that the belt stops for every detected leaflet, so your staff can remove it right away, instead of having those leaflets accumulate on the belt, which would most definitely lead to more issues down the road.
Also pssible would be to deactivate the "stop on xproduct error" option, so the belt will not stop with an alarm for every detected XP, and tagged totes would go to the manual check station. In this case you would have to clean the central belt of any stuck leaflets regularly (once a week f.e.).

In the end it will have to be determined by you if you prefer the XP detection to be less precise, and therefore accept a higher risk of false negative detection, if you want to "stop on xp" alarm to be disabled,
or if you want to keep it as it is (probably the safest option when it comes to quality control and maintenance of the central belt in my opinion).
I hope this answers you questions! If you want to discuss possible changes in detail, please don't hesitate to give us a call. The ticket moves onto status "Waiting for customer response" until I hear from you again. Please get in touch with us once you have made a decision on how to proceed.

Best regards

 

  
______________________
